label: Original-phase B-group token (c,r,3,f,t,d,a,e,y) after a prefix dominated by A-group tokens (2,0,w,n,g,q,u,h,b)
explanation: Fires almost only while the original tokens are being read (92% of mass; t>=2, peaking at t=3-6) and on the <DEL> step (7.5% of mass). It is essentially silent during the copy phase and at t=0-1. It behaves like a graded linear threshold over two token groups. The current input pushes it up when it is c, r, 3, f, t, d, a, e or y (weaker for j, x, s, v). Earlier inputs push it up when they are 2, 0, w, n, g, q, u, h or b, and down when they are themselves from the c/r/3/f group. The largest activations (about 0.29) come in sequences that open with several A-group tokens (e.g. 2 0 w g q ...) followed by B-group tokens. In such sequences, consecutive B tokens and <DEL> all fire. When a sequence opens with B-group tokens (e.g. c r d y x a), it stays silent. First occurrences of a token account for most of the mass, but repeats can also fire. The predicate is a binarised approximation of this graded weighting: dev F1 is about 0.52, and it misses low-weight tokens and borderline sums, so the description is incomplete.
